layout_details.content: ## 5.12 Code
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Technical content such as programming language code, pseudo-code, schemas and DTDs or markup fragments should be tagged as <code>. Whitespace will be preserved within <code>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Preformatted text, which may contain emphasis elements for syntax coloring, or it may contain an external link to a binary executable file, can be included in <code>].
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Attributes of <code>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @id
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @code-type - typically a descriptive word such as "pseudo-code" or "scripting" that describes the type of language (not the name of the language) in which the code is written.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @code-version - Version of the program code that is shown inside the <code> element, for example, "25.1 second patch"
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @executable - Indicates whether or not the code snippet to which the attribute is attached is intended for direct execution
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @language - Code Language
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @language-version - Code Language Version
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - @platforms - Platform on which the code is intended to run, for example, "Mac OS X".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Authors are encouraged to make use of these attributes wherever possible and applicable. In ISO and IEC documents, however, these are not used today. They will be in the future.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: CDATA should be used to avoid parsing XML examples included in the text.

layout_details.content: ## 6 Tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Tables are coded using XHTML. The NISO STS framework also allows CALS, but this format is not used by ISO or IEC. This document does not explain CALS tagging.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Further detailed information on capturing content within tables is included in.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Nested tables are not permitted.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Editorial note
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Nested tables may appear in legacy documents, but are deprecated.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Borders and shading should be represented using the style attribute of the respective table element. The width of table columns should be defined using @width inside <col> within <table>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## ISO
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In ISO, the width of each column is captured as a percentage, but the overall table width is set in <table> @width in absolute number of pixels.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<table-wrap id="tab_B.1" position="float">

<label>Table B.1</label>

<caption>

<title>Dimensional requirements for different vehicle types within the Japanese

regulation</title>

</caption>

<table width="652">

<col width="25%"/>

<col width="25%"/>

<col width="25%"/>

<col width="25%"/>

<thead>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In IEC, the width of each column is captured as a percentage. No absolute number of pixels is indicated for table width.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<table-wrap id="tab-1">

<label>Table 1</label>

<caption>

<title>Spectrum analyser parameters</title></caption>

<table>

<colgroup>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="12%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="22%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="14%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="10%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="10%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="18%"/>

<col align="center" valign="middle" width="14%"></colgroup>

<thead>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.3 Layout of content inside cells
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The text content of cells should be coded according to the instructions for coding text, except that spacing and line breaks should be handled differently.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Alignment of content within columns should be done using row subdivisions,rather than line breaks inside one row.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - The presence of merged or split cells should be reflected in the coding by using column or row span tags (see Merged cells).
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Alignment of text in a cell should be reflected in the alignment coding, rather than by using spacing.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.4 Formal vs informal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A formal table consists of at least a label and a table, normally also a title, captured within <table-wrap>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: An informal table does not have a caption (label and title) and is captured as a <table> in <array>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.5 Informal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Structured information presented in tabular format, but which does not have a label, is captured using <table> inside <array>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.6 Formal tables
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.6.1 General
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: In ISO and IEC documents, all table elements are coded in <table> within <table-wrap>, using XHTML.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## Attribute of <table-wrap>
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: @id - usually contains the number of the table (e.g. "tab-1" or "tab_1").
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 6.6.2 Designation
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A table designation is normally placed above formal tables, e.g. "Table 1 - Alphabetical list of definitions".
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: The XHTML table model requires the two elements that make up the designation, label ("Table 1") and title ("Alphabetical list of definitions "), to be tagged inside two different hierarchical elements:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Directly below <table-wrap>, use <label> to code the label, without the trailing dash and without spaces.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: - Then, inside a <caption> element, use <title> to code the title.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For example:
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<table-wrap id="tab-1">

<label>Table 1</label>

<caption>

<title>Alphabetical list of definitions</title></caption>

<table>

<colgroup>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7 Formulae and equations
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.1 Elements and attributes
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: A full formula/equation that is separate from the surrounding text is coded using <disp-formula>. If a full formula/equation is embedded in the flow of the text that surrounds it, it should be captured in <inline-formula>.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Symbols for variable quantities without operators that appear within the flow of text should be coded as normal text, formatted as they appear in the text, including font information (e.g. TNR). Symbols should be captured in UTF-8 codepoint.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: Numbered formulae usually are separated from the text and labelled with a number in parentheses, e.g. (1). This number is usually sequential and numbered independently throughout the document, irrespective the numbering of any containing clauses. Numbered formulae contained in annexes are prefixed by the annex letter.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For numbered formulae, the formula number should also be captured as a <label> within the <dispformula>, e.g.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
```html

<disp-formula id="formula_1">

    <label>(1)</label>

    <mml:math id="mml_m1">

        ...

    </mml:math>

</disp-formula>

```
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: ## 7.2 Numbered formulae
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content: For numbered formulae, the formula ID should match the label of the formula.
layout_details.label: text

layout_details.content:
ISO

For example, formula_1 for Formula 1.

```html

<disp-formula id="formula_1">

<label>(1)</label>

```
